title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken with Spinach
description: This Tuscan chicken has creamy comfort without the heavy cream, thanks to a mix of low-fat milk and Greek yogurt. With lean protein, fiber-rich spinach, and no added sugars, it’s a balanced dish that will help you reach your blood glucose (blood sugar) goals. It’s a great choice if you’re looking for something hearty, flavorful, and diabetes friendly.
ingredients: 12 oz low sodium chicken broth (fat free)
1/2 cup fresh basil (torn, plus more for serving)
steps: Sprinkle the chicken breasts with the pepper, garlic powder, and oregano. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chicken and sear until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 165 degrees F, about 4–5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.

In the same skillet, add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Pour in the chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits. Stir in the milk, sun-dried tomatoes, and red pepper flakes. Simmer for 2–3 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and Parmesan cheese, cooking until spinach wilts, about 1–2 minutes.

Remove the pan from the heat once the sauce is finished simmering. In a small bowl, mix ¼ cup plain Greek yogurt with 1–2 Tbsp of the warm sauce to temper it. Slowly stir the tempered yogurt into the pan, mixing gently until fully incorporated.
Return the chicken to the pan. Spoon the sauce over the top. Add half of the basil and simmer for 1–2 minutes to heat through.
Serve with additional fresh basil on top.

title: Chicken and Dumplings
description: Try these chicken and dumplings for a budget-friendly family dinner. Add a side of roasted green beans to complete your meal.
ingredients: 8 cup low sodium chicken broth (fat-free, low-sodium)
steps: Mix the flours, baking soda, baking powder, sage, salt (optional), and pepper in a medium bowl. Add yogurt, egg, and water and knead to make a slightly sticky dough. Cover the bowl and set aside.
Add cooking spray and olive oil to a large soup pot over medium high heat. Add the onion, carrots, celery, and mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes or until the vegetables are softened.
Add the chicken and broth, and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer for 5 minutes.
Roll the dough out into an 8 inch disk that is 1/2-inch thick. Cut the dough into 1 inch pieces and drop the dumplings into the simmering broth. Stir frequently until all the dumplings are added.
Simmer the dumplings for 10 minutes and serve.

title: Roasted Pepper and Caper Salad
description: This Italian inspired salad is a great way to add some non-starchy vegetables to your plate. Lower in carbs, but high in taste, your whole family with enjoy this fresh and healthy choice.
steps: Preheat the oven broiler. Place the whole bell peppers on a baking sheet and broil, turning occasionally, until the skin is charred and blistered. Remove from the oven and let them cool. Once cool, peel off the skin, remove seeds, and slice into strips.
In a bowl, combine the roasted pepper strips, drained capers, sliced Kalamata olives, and chopped fresh parsley.
In a small bowl, whisk together extra-virgin olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the roasted pepper mixture. Toss gently to combine, ensuring even coating.
Let the salad marinate for at least 15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

title: Chicken and Roasted Pepper Lettuce Cups
description: This recipe featured in: Designed for One! by Nancy S. Hughes.
ingredients: 1/3 cup chickpeas (garbanzo beans) (no salt added, rinsed and drained)
2 leaves romaine or Boston lettuce leaves
steps: Heat a small nonstick skillet over medium heat. Coat both sides of the chicken with cooking spray and cook 4 minutes on each side, or until no longer pink in the center. Place on cutting board, let cool 2–3 minutes, and chop.
Meanwhile, combine the remaining ingredients, except the lettuce leaves, in a bowl.
To assemble, line each leaf with the chopped chicken and top with the red pepper mixture.

title: Flourless Brownies
description: Rich and decadent, these Flourless Brownies are an indulgent dessert that’s diabetes friendly.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line an 8x8 inch baking pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang for easy removal.

Place the vegetable oil and carob chips in a medium bowl set over a pot of simmering water. Melt the carob chips with the vegetable oil, stirring slowly and continuously. Once melted, remove the bowl from the pot and dry the bottom of it.
Whisk in the sugar substitute and then the eggs one at a time until the batter is smooth.
Add the vanilla extract and cocoa powder and stir to combine.
Spread the batter evenly in the baking dish. Bake for 15-18 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Let cool completely in the pan.
Use the parchment sling and lift the brownies out of the pan. Slice and serve.

title: Falafel Salad with Lemon-Herb Vinaigrette
description: This salad is loaded with crisp veggies, warm herb-packed chickpea patties (falafel), and a zesty lemon vinaigrette for a satisfying meal. Baked instead of fried, the falafel keeps things lighter while still delivering fiber and plant-based protein. With no added sugar and plenty of carbs that will digest slowly, it's a diabetes-friendly option for a hearty lunch or dinner.
ingredients: 1 cup canned chickpeas (no salt added, drained and rinsed)
steps: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F.

Place chickpeas in a food processor with 1 small yellow onion, 2 cloves garlic, herbs and spices (1 cup fresh parsley leaves, 1 cup fresh cilantro leaves, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp ground coriander, ¼ tsp salt, ¼ tsp black pepper). Pulse until the mixture is coarse and holds together when pressed.
Add baking powder and flour, pulsing briefly to combine. Chill for at least 1 hour.
Form into small balls or patties (about 1–1.5 inches wide). Place on a baking sheet and repeat to make 12–16 falafel balls.

Spray the falafel balls with cooking spray. Bake on the bottom rack of the oven for 15 minutes. Turn the oven down to 350 degrees F and move the baking sheet to the top rack. Bake for an additional 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a small jar or bowl, combine olive oil, lemon juice, mustard, remaining garlic, and 1 tbsp chopped fresh dill. Shake or whisk until emulsified. Season with 1/8 tsp salt and 1/8 tsp pepper.
To assemble, divide romaine, tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and ¼ cup fresh chopped parsley between bowls.
Drizzle with the lemon-herb vinaigrette and toss to coat. Top with warm falafel and serve immediately.

title: Sweet Potato and Spinach Chicken Tacos
description: Unexpected taco fillings are all the rage on the food truck scene. Make these rich and savory versions at home!
ingredients: 1/2 cup pico de gallo or salsa
steps: In a large nonstick pan, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the garlic and sauté for 30 seconds. Add the spinach and sauté for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the sweet potato, cumin, black pepper, and water to the pan. Sauté for 2 minutes. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the chicken to the pan and mix to incorporate. Heat for 2 minutes.
Fill each tortilla with 1/4 of the chicken and sweet potato mixture. Top with 1 Tsp. of sour cream and 2 Tbsp. of pico de gallo.

title: Coconut Almond Chicken Tenders with Sweet Spicy Sauce
description: Sweet coconut and almond pair perfectly with a spicy sauce to take these chicken tenders to the next level.
ingredients: 2 whole boneless, skinless chicken breasts (cut into 8-1 inch strips)
steps: Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and cover a sheet pan with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs to break them up.
In another medium bowl, whisk together the panko, shredded coconut, chopped almonds, and garlic powder.
Dip each chicken strip first in egg and then in coconut mixture, making sure to coat it well with the crumbs.
Place on the baking sheet and bake until the tenders have an internal temperature of 165 degrees F, about 15 minutes.
For the dipping sauce, whisk together apricot jam, garlic chili sauce and kosher salt. Thin with 1-2 tablespoons of water and strain, if desired.
Serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Country Stuffed Summer Squash
description: Using packaged cornbread stuffing mix makes this side dish simple to pull together. It’s a flavorful summer side dish you can make any night of the week. For a fun appetizer use baby squash and double the number or cut the regular squash into 2-inch pieces before serving.
ingredients: 2 large zucchini or yellow summer squash (halved lengthwise, 12 ounces total; use any variety, such as yellow, scallop, or zucchini)
1 cup red or green bell pepper (chopped)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Scoop out and coarsely chop the squash pulp.

Place a medium nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until hot. Coat the skillet with nonstick cooking spray and add the squash pulp and bell pepper. Cook 4 minutes or until the pepper is tender-crisp, stirring frequently.

Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in the water and margarine. Add the stuffing mix and stir gently with a fork. Spoon 1/2 cup stuffing into each squash half. Press down gently so the stuffing will adhere.
Recoat the skillet with nonstick cooking spray, arrange the stuffed squash in the skillet, cover tightly, and bake 30 minutes or until the squash is tender when pierced with a fork.

title: Baked Chai Apple Chips
description: Baked apple chips are a delicious crunchy and sweet treat. This recipe adds chai flavoring, a warming blend of spices that’s perfect for a healthy fall and winter weather snack.
ingredients: 2 med apple (sweet varieties like Fuji or Honeycrisp)
steps: Preheat your oven to 200 degrees F and line two baking sheets with parchment paper. You can also lightly grease the parchment paper with cooking spray to prevent sticking.

Wash and core the apples, removing the seeds and stems. You can leave the peel on for added texture and nutrients. Using a mandoline slicer or a sharp knife, thinly slice the apples into rounds, aiming for slices of about 1/8-inch thickness. Make sure they are consistently thin for even baking.
In a small bowl, mix the ground cinnamon, ground cardamom, ground ginger, ground cloves, and ground nutmeg to create a chai spice blend.

Lay out the apple slices on the prepared baking sheets in a single layer, ensuring they do not overlap. Sprinkle the chai spice blend evenly over the apple slices. You can use your fingers or a shaker to distribute the spices evenly.

Place the baking sheets in the preheated oven and bake for about 2 hours. You'll want to check the apple chips occasionally to prevent overcooking. The chips are done when they become crisp but not burnt. They will become even crispier as they cool.

title: Edamame with Lemon Juice
description: Nutrition information for edamame with lemon juice
steps: Drizzle lemon juice over edamame.

title: Whole Grain Bread or Toast
description: Nutrition information for Whole Grain Bread or Toast

title: Cilantro Lime Rice and Black Bean Bowl
description: Enjoy this Tex-Mex meal that is both vegan and diabetes friendly. Packed with colorful and nutrient-rich veggies, this meal is easy enough to prepare for a healthy weeknight dinner.
ingredients: ½ (15 oz) can black beans (No added salt, drained and rinsed)
steps: In a large bowl, combine the cooked brown rice, black beans, corn, diced red bell pepper, chopped red onion, and fresh cilantro.
In a small bowl, juice the two limes. Add the olive oil, ground cumin, chili powder, and kosher salt. Whisk until well combined.
Pour the dressing over the rice and bean mixture. Toss well to ensure even coating.
Allow the flavors to meld for a few minutes before serving.
Top with avocado slices, if desired.

title: Huevos Rancheros
description: Huevos rancheros is a simple, hearty dish that’s full of bold flavor. Eggs are served on warm tortillas and topped with a savory tomato-based sauce. It’s a satisfying choice for breakfast or any meal, combining protein, veggies, and great taste in every bite.
ingredients: 1 can canned diced tomatoes (14.5-ounce, no-salt-added, drained)
steps: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F.
Place the tortillas on the baking sheet and bake 3 minutes on each side.

Meanwhile, place the tomatoes, cumin, cayenne, and salt in a medium non-stick skillet and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook, covered, for 3 minutes or until slightly thickened. Break one egg into a measuring cup. Carefully slide egg onto the tomato mixture. Repeat with the remaining eggs. Simmer gently over medium heat, covered, for 2 1/2 to 3 minutes or until the egg whites are completely set and the yolks just begin to thicken slightly.
Place a tortilla on each plate. Top with the tomato mixture and eggs and sprinkle with cheese and cilantro.

title: Winter Salad with Citrus
description: Salads aren’t just for summer, they’re for winter too especially when you can throw in some citrus fruits, which are in season for the winter!
steps: Combine the dressing ingredients in a bowl.
Combine the greens, grapefruit, oranges, onion and walnuts. Add dressing and toss to coat.

title: Whole Grain Pasta, cooked
description: Nutrition information for 1/2 cup cooked whole grain pasta

title: Air Fryer Spicy Green Beans
description: Spice up your green beans with this air fried dish that can serve as a low-carb appetizer, snack, or side dish. Crispy panko and spicy chili paste add flavor and crunch. Cooking in the air fryer gives you the satisfying crunch of fried food, without all the added fat of deep frying. Click here for more air fryer recipes!
steps: Place the green beans in a medium bowl and toss with the olive oil, chili garlic paste, panko bread crumbs, and salt.
Place the green beans in the air fryer basket. Set the temperature to 400° F and air fry for 4 minutes. Shake the air fryer basket. Air fry for an additional 5 to 7 minutes. Serve warm.

title: Salt-Free Gluten-Free Crackers
description: Nutrition information for salt-free gluten-free crackers

title: Quinoa Pilaf
description: This Quinoa Pilaf is a nutrition powerhouse because quinoa provides more protein than other grains and it’s also a good source of potassium an dietary fiber.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cup white (button) mushrooms (wiped clean and chopped)
3 cup low sodium chicken broth (fat-free, reduced-sodium)
steps: Add the olive oil to a medium saucepan. Sauté onion and celery over medium-high heat and cook about 3 minutes or until the onions are clear.
Add mushrooms and cook until brown. Add the quinoa to the pan and stir for 1-2 minutes.
Slowly add the chicken broth, salt, pepper and thyme and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer. Cook 15 minutes and fluff with a fork when done.

title: Peach, 1 medium
description: Nutrition information for a Peach

title: Grilled Salmon with Mango and Tomato Salsa
description:
Mango and other fruit can add a slight sweetness to any salsa. It works particularly well with this slightly spicy salmon dish. Grilling salmon fillets with the skin on makes them easier to flip and helps prevent sticking. Oiling your grill grates can also prevent sticking: dip a balled up paper towel in oil and rubbing lightly over clean grill grates.

You could also cook the salmon in the oven: Preheat oven to 425°F and bake the salmon in a shallow baking pan for about 10 minutes or until cooked through.
serving_size: 1 salmon filet (4 oz) with 1/2 cup salsa
steps: Preheat the grill to medium high heat.
In a small bowl, combine chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, cinnamon, and salt. Sprinkle the spice mixture evenly over the salmon fillets.

Lightly oil the grill grates with the canola oil. Place the salmon on the grill, skin side down. Cook uncovered for 7 to 8 minutes, turning halfway through. The salmon is done when it flakes easily with a fork.
While salmon is cooking, combine mango, tomatoes, cilantro, and half of the lemon juice in a medium bowl.
Remove salmon from grill and spritz with remaining lemon juice. Serve each fillet with 1/2 cup salsa.

title: Budget-Friendly Mediterranean Fish Stew
description: This Mediterranean fish stew costs a little more than $10 for 4 servings, but it can be a real treat and is great for the chilly winter weather!
ingredients: 1 med red bell pepper (seeded and diced)
1 (28-oz can) canned crushed tomatoes (no salt added)
steps: Add olive oil to a soup pot over medium heat. Add onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic, basil and oregano. Sauté until onions begin to turn clear.
Add crushed tomato and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 10 minutes or until vegetables are soft.
Gently stir in cod and shrimp and cook for 5 minutes or until seafood is cooked through.

title: Minestrone Pasta Bowl
description: This is a vegan, vegetarian, and low-fat recipe featuring Ready for a hearty, plant-based lunch that is full of mediterranean flavor? This chickpea pasta bowl is filled with colorful veggies, chickpeas and flavorful herbs and spices. It’s an easy healthy and filling lunch idea.
ingredients: 1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes (no salt added)
1 (16 ounce) can canned chickpeas (low sodium, rinsed and drained)
4 oz box chickpea penne pasta (about 2 cups)
steps: Heat olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add onions and carrots and sauté until they start to soften, about 4 minutes.
Add garlic and sauté an additional 1 minute, being careful not to burn it.
Stir in the dry spices and coat the vegetables. Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, white wine vinegar, and broth.
Add the pasta and stir it well. Cover the pan and allow it to cook for 6–7 minutes, until the pasta is just starting to soften.
Add the kale and continue cooking for another 2 minutes, just long enough to wilt the kale and finish cooking the pasta.

title: Sheet Pan Cheesy Mini Meatloaves with Bell Peppers & Onions
description: Elevate your weeknight dinners with these Sheet Pan Cheesy Mini Meatloaves made with a colorful medley of bell peppers and onions. This Very-Low-Carbohydrate Meal Pattern recipe is not only easy to prepare, it’s packed with flavor and nutrients, making it a perfect choice for a healthy and satisfying dinner the whole family will enjoy.
ingredients: 6 oz block fat free mozzarella cheese (cut into 12 slices)
steps: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F. Line a large baking sheet pan with aluminum foil.
Place turkey, egg, breadcrumbs, half of the Italian seasoning, and black pepper in a medium bowl. Mix with your hands until the meatloaf mixture is well combined.
Form the beef mixture into 12 short logs, approximately 3-inches long. Transfer to one half of the baking sheet.

Spread the bell peppers and onion on the unused side of the baking sheet. Drizzle the vegetables with oil, sprinkle with the remaining seasoning, and toss to coat evenly. Arrange them in a single layer.
Place the baking sheet in the oven and roast, stirring the vegetables midway, until the meatloaves are nearly cooked and the vegetables are tender when pierced with a fork, about 15–20 minutes.

Take the baking sheet out of the oven when the meatloaves are almost done. Lay slices of cheese on top of each meatloaf. Return the sheet to the oven and bake until the meatloaves are fully cooked and the cheese has melted, about 2–3 more minutes.

title: Pan-Roasted Padron Peppers with Salt
description: Pan-roasted Padron peppers with salt is a simple and delightful dish that highlights the unique flavor of Padron peppers. These small green peppers are known for their mild, slightly sweet flavor, with the occasional spicy kick.
steps: Heat a large, heavy skillet or frying pan over medium-high heat. Add 1–2 tablespoons of olive oil, depending on your preference and the size of your skillet.

When the oil is hot and shimmering, add the Padron peppers to the skillet. You can leave them whole with the stems on. Let the peppers cook, undisturbed, for about 3–5 minutes or until they start to blister and char. Use tongs to turn them occasionally, so they cook evenly.
Once the Padron peppers are tender, blistered, and slightly charred, remove them from the skillet and transfer to a serving plate.
While the peppers are still hot, generously sprinkle them with coarse sea salt.

title: Whole Wheat Dinner Roll
description: Nutrition information for whole wheat dinner roll

title: Spinach Salad with Goat Cheese & Beets
description: This classic spinach salad with goat cheese and beets is colorful, flavorful, and full of nutrients. Spinach is the star of the show, a vitamin-packed vegetable that is a great addition to any diabetes-friendly diet. The honey and Dijon mustard dressing adds a touch of sweetness and takes these flavors to the next level. Wanting to add more spinach to your diet? Try out these recipes! • Easy Spinach Ricotta Enchiladas • Spinach Artichoke Stuffed Portobellos
steps: Scrub the beets and trim and discard the tops. Place in a saucepan or pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until fork-tender, 30–45 minutes.
Remove from water and let cool, then peel and slice into wedges.
In a large bowl, whisk together the canola oil, water, honey, and Dijon mustard. Add spinach and toss to coat.
Add beets, goat cheese, and pine nuts. Toss again gently.

title: Caesar-Style Salad with Rustic Croutons
description: Who doesn’t love Caesar salad? This salad makes a great nonstarchy vegetable side that you can enjoy with just about any entrée!
serving_size: 1 cup salad + 2 tbsp dressing + 1/2 cup croutons
ingredients: 2 slice whole wheat bread or French bread (torn into 1/2-inch pieces)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.

In a small mixing bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, mayonnaise, garlic powder, salt (optional) and pepper (optional) to taste. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 1 hour in order to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, place the bread pieces on a baking sheet and bake 8 minutes or until slightly firm. Remove from heat and cool slightly.
Place mixed greens in a salad bowl, add dressing and cheese, and toss gently, yet thoroughly to coat. Season lightly with salt and pepper, if desired. Add croutons, toss gently and serve immediately.
*Note: Optional salt and pepper is not included in the nutrition information above.

title: Lentils and Greens with Apples
description: Hearty lentils meet the vibrant flavors of leafy greens and the sweet crunch of apples in this lunch recipe. This nutrient-rich dish not only satisfies your palate with its diverse textures, it’s also a great option for a diabetes-friendly eating plan.
ingredients: 1 cup green or brown lentils (rinsed and drained)
steps: In a medium saucepan, combine dry lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15–20 minutes or until lentils are tender. Drain any excess liquid.
In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent.
Add minced garlic to the skillet and sauté for an additional 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the chopped mixed greens and cook until wilted.
Add cooked lentils to the skillet, stirring to combine with the greens.
In a small bowl, whisk together apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, salt and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the lentil and greens mixture. Stir to coat evenly.
Gently fold in the thinly sliced apples. Sprinkle chopped walnuts over the top and finish with the avocado.

title: Sheet Pan Garlic Shrimp and Asparagus
description: Sheet pan dinners are quick and easy meals without a lot of clean up. This Garlic Shrimp and Asparagus version is ready to eat in 20 minutes!
ingredients: 1 lbs shrimp (large, peeled and deveined, not packed in solution)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the shrimp and asparagus. Add olive oil, minced garlic, red pepper flakes (if using), kosher salt, and black pepper. Toss everything together until the shrimp and asparagus are evenly coated.
Spread the shrimp and asparagus in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Roast in the preheated oven for approximately 8–10 minutes or until the shrimp are opaque and the asparagus is tender but still crisp.

title: Tofu “Egg” Muffins with Sundried Tomato and Basil
description: This is a vegetarian, low carb, and very low carb recipe featuring tofu “egg” muffins which are a flavorful, plant-based twist on classic breakfast bites, packed with sun-dried tomatoes, basil, and a touch of turmeric for color and warmth. Chickpea flour and tofu provide protein and fiber without the cholesterol or saturated fat of traditional egg muffins. They’re a great make-ahead option for people with diabetes, offering steady energy and balanced nutrition in every bite.
serving_size: 2 muffins per serving, makes 8 muffins total
ingredients: 14 oz firm tofu (1 block, drained and patted dry)
1/4 cup unsweetened almond milk (or unsweetened soy milk)
1/4 cup red bell pepper (finely chopped [optional, for color and crunch])
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Lightly grease a nonstick muffin pan or use silicone muffin cups.
In a food processor or blender, combine tofu, plant-based milk, chickpea flour, olive oil, turmeric, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Blend until smooth and creamy.
Transfer the tofu mixture to a large bowl. Fold in the sun-dried tomatoes, basil, and chopped bell pepper.
Spoon the mixture evenly into 8 muffin cups, smoothing the tops.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, or until the tops are firm and lightly golden. Let cool for 5 minutes in the pan before removing.
Serve warm, or cool completely and refrigerate for up to 4 days.

title: Roasted and Spiced Chickpeas
description: This high-fiber snack is a much healthier choice than chips and is a great alternative for those with nut allergies. Place in small bowls or ramekins at your next party. Eat them as a snack or use them as a crunchy topping on soups or salads.
ingredients: 1 (15.5-oz) can chickpeas (garbanzo beans) (rinsed and drained (dry well))
steps: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray.
In a medium bowl mix together garbanzo beans, 1 Tbsp. olive oil, cinnamon, cumin, chili powder and salt.
Spread garbanzo bean mixture evenly on baking sheet. Bake for 40–45 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until beans are crispy and dry.
Remove from oven and place hot beans in a medium bowl. Add 1 Tbsp. olive oil and brown sugar substitute. Mix well.
Pour beans on parchment paper and allow to cool for 20 minutes.

title: Parsley Lemon Chickpea Salad
description: With plant-based protein from chickpeas, this recipe fits a vegetarian, vegan or low carb eating pattern. Pair this chickpea salad with a leafy green salad for a delicious meal the whole family will love.
ingredients: 1 whole lemon (zest and juice from lemon)
steps: Place the diced onion in a bowl of cold water for 10 minutes, then drain.
In a medium bowl, combine the chickpeas, olive oil, lemon zest and juice, parsley, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Add the drained onions and stir again to combine. Taste and adjust with more lemon, salt, or pepper, if necessary.

title: Chicken and Vegetable Soup
description: Soup is a healthy meal that you can load with lots of veggies. If desired, you can add some brown or wild rice to this dish, but add some extra water. This soup would go well with our Orange and Walnut Salad
steps: Add the oil to a large soup pot or dutch oven and heat over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and sear for 4 minutes on each side. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add the carrots, celery, and mushrooms to the same pot and sauté over medium-high heat for 5 minutes.
Add the remaining ingredients and add the chicken back to the pot. Bring to a boil; reduce the heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pot and shred or cut up. Add the chicken back to the pot; stir.

title: Sage Stuffing
description: Here’s a stuffing recipe that’s on the healthier side but will still thrill your guests. Our Sage Stuffing uses whole grain bread, omega-3 rich walnuts and cranberries to give it a holiday twist.
ingredients: 1 loaf (about 2 lbs) day-old whole-grain bread (crusts removed, cut into small cubes)
1/2 bunch fresh sage (stems removed, coarsely chopped)
1/2 cup dried cranberries or cherries (coarsely chopped)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375° F. Add the bread to a large bowl.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onions and celery, and sauté for 3 minutes. Add the walnuts and sauté for 2 minutes. Add in the sage and cook for 1 minute.

Add the onion-sage mixture to the bread. Pour the hot chicken broth and egg over the onion-sage, and mix well (until moist). Add in the cranberries or cherries. Season well with salt and pepper. Add the mixture to a large casserole dish, and sprinkle with paprika. Bake for about 40-45 minutes, or until the top is browned and crusty.

title: White Bean Veggie Chili
description: Enjoy the hearty and comforting flavors of this Vegan Meal Pattern White Bean Veggie Chili, a delicious blend of white beans, bell peppers, zucchini, and a mix of warming spices. This vegetarian chili is both satisfying and healthy, perfect for a cozy dinner.
ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans cannellini beans (reduced sodium, drained and rinsed)
14 1/2 oz canned diced tomatoes (no salt added)
steps: Preheat a large pot over medium heat.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic, veggies, and spices and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 7–8 minutes.
Add beans, broth, and tomatoes to the pot. Stir to combine the chili and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer, stirring occasionally, until veggies and beans are soft, about 30 minutes.
To serve, divide chili between bowls and top with parsley.

title: Arroz con Leche (Rice Custard)
description: If you are Latin, then you have most certainly had this delicious dessert! What you probably have not had is a diabetes-friendly version that you will love just as much as the traditional dish. This guiltless version is sugar-free and features extra fiber from brown rice and flax seeds.
steps: Prepare the rice according to the package directions.

Combine the cooked rice, milk, water, sugar substitute, orange peel, cinnamon stick, flaxseeds, and cloves in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium low and simmer, stirring often, until the rice pudding is thick and creamy, about 20 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Remove and discard the orange peel, cinnamon stick, and cloves. Stir in vanilla and ground cinnamon.

title: Orange Creamsicle Smoothie
description: If you love orange creamsicle popsicles, you’ll love this smoothie! Designed to be diabetes-friendly, this recipe uses protein-rich Greek yogurt to make for a satisfying smoothie.
steps: Add the orange, banana, orange juice, yogurt, and vanilla in a blender. Blend until smooth.
Pour into two glasses. Enjoy immediately.

title: Cooked Oatmeal
description: Nutrition information for oatmeal

title: Baked Fish Fillets with Thyme-Dijon Topping
description: Serve up these tasty, baked fish fillets with some roasted sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts. It would make a diabetes-friendly, yet elegant dish to make for your sweetie on a special occasion!
ingredients: 4 (4 ounce) fillets grouper or other mild fish fillets (rinsed and patted dry)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Lightly spray a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Place the fish on the baking sheet. Bake for 18-20 minutes, or until the fish flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, stir together the remaining ingredients.
Spread the margarine mixture over the fish.

title: Holiday Veggie Platter with Hummus – Quick Recipe
description: It’s amazing how people will eat more veggies when they are in front of them, displayed well and served with a good dip. Hummus is a healthy dip made from chickpeas and comes in a variety of flavors.
steps: Arrange vegetables on a large, round platter. Alternate red vegetables with green vegetables in a circle on platter.
Place hummus in a small bowl in center of platter.

title: Pasta Fagioli
description: This hearty Italian soup makes a great lunch or side dish with your holiday meal. To cut down on prep time, chop the onion, garlic, celery, and carrots quickly using a food processor.
steps: Coat a large soup pot with cooking spray over high heat. Add bacon and sauté until crisp.
Reduce heat to medium and add onion, garlic, celery, and carrots. Sauté about 5-7 minutes or until vegetables begin to brown. Add broth and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in beans, tomatoes, parsley, basil, and pepper and simmer for 10 minutes. Add the pasta and continue to simmer for 10-15 minutes or until pasta is al dente.
Serve soup in a bowl sprinkled with Parmesan cheese.

title: Lemon Garlic Shrimp Skewers
description: These Lemon Garlic Shrimp Skewers are versatile and can be served alongside a salad, over brown rice, or with your favorite veggies. The combination of lemon and garlic adds a bright and savory kick to the grilled shrimp.
steps: If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for at least 15 minutes to prevent burning during grilling.
Zest and juice one of the lemons. Thinly slice the other.
In a bowl, combine the olive oil, minced garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, dried oregano, rosemary, and black pepper.
Add the peeled and deveined shrimp to the marinade, making sure they are well coated. Let them marinate for at least 15 minutes
Preheat your grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Thread the marinated shrimp onto the skewers, along with one or two lemon slices per skewer.
Place the shrimp skewers on the preheated grill and cook for about 2–3 minutes per side or until the shrimp are fully cooked and develop a light char.

title: Veggie Egg Fu Yung
description: Try this meal for a unique Asian-inspired dish that’s also easy on the budget. It’s great for breakfast, lunch, or dinner!
ingredients: 2 sprays, 0.50 g nonstick cooking spray (divided use)
1 cup canned bean sprouts (drained and rinsed)
steps: Add the cooking spray and canola oil to a non-stick sauté pan over medium heat. Add the mushrooms, zucchini, and onion. Sauté until the mushrooms are dry and the onions turn clear, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the bean sprouts. Sauté 2-3 more minutes. Set aside to cool.
In a medium bowl, whisk the egg substitute and egg together. Whisk in the flour and then stir in the vegetable mixture and salt (optional). Mix well.

Over medium-high heat, re-spray nonstick sauté pan with cooking spray and pour the batter by heaping 1/2 cup to form patties. Cook well on both sides until golden brown, about 4-5 minutes per side. Remove the patties from the pan and set aside.

In a small bowl, combine the cornstarch, low- or no-calorie sweetener, soy sauce, and chicken broth. Mix well. Add this mixture to the hot pan and bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes to make a gravy.
Pour the gravy over patties and serve hot.

title: Sheet Pan Herby Salmon and Asparagus
description: Sheet pan meals are quick, easy, and don’t have a lot of clean up. What could be better? This salmon and asparagus version is diabetes-friendly and packed with omega-3 fatty acids, making it a healthy choice for a weeknight meal.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and cover a sheet pan with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, chopped dill, lemon zest, lemon juice, kosher salt, and pepper.
Place the salmon filets and asparagus on a sheet pan and spoon the herb mixture on top of each filet.
Bake until the salmon is cooked to an internal temperature of 145°F, about 20 minutes and the asparagus is tender.

title: Roasted Radishes with Rosemary
description: Experience the unique delight of roasted radishes, a low-carb side dish that transforms these vibrant roots into a savory, diabetes-friendly indulgence. Best of all? It’s easy enough to put together for any weeknight meal!
steps: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F and cover a sheet pan in parchment paper.
Toss the radish halves with olive oil, dried rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Roast for 15–20 minutes until tender.
Serve warm. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley if desired.

title: Pumpkin Crisp
description: Pumpkin Crisp is a delightful fall dessert that captures the warm and spiced flavors of pumpkin in a comforting, crumbly topping. This diabetes-friendly version is perfect for a healthier holiday dessert.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line a 9 x 9” baking pan with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the pumpkin puree, eggs, zero-calorie maple syrup, almond milk, vanilla extract, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, ground nutmeg, ground ginger, and salt.
Pour the pumpkin mixture into the prepared pan and spread in an even layer.
In another bowl, combine the oats, almond flour, chopped pecans, 1 tsp cinnamon, and vegetable oil. Stir until the mixture is crumbly.
Sprinkle the oat mixture evenly over the top of the pumpkin.
Bake until the pumpkin filling is set and the oat topping is golden brown, about 35 minutes.
Let it cool for 10 minutes and then serve warm.

title: Gluten-Free Frozen Raspberry Yogurt Clusters
description: A simple, gluten-free snack that combines creamy nonfat Greek yogurt with sweet, tart raspberries and freezes into bite-sized clusters. They’re refreshing, high protein, and perfect for a cool treat that feels indulgent but stays nutrient dense.
steps: Line a small plate or tray with parchment paper.
In a bowl, gently fold 1 cup raspberries into ¾ cup nonfat Greek yogurt, keeping some berries whole for texture.
Spoon small dollops of the mixture onto the parchment to form clusters.
Freeze for 1–2 hours, or until fully firm.
Enjoy straight from the freezer.

title: Egg Whites, 1/2 cup
description: Nutrition information for cooking egg whites.
steps: Lightly coat a small nonstick skillet with cooking spray and place it over medium heat.
Pour 1/2 cup liquid egg whites into the warm skillet.
Let the egg whites cook undisturbed for 1–2 minutes until they begin to set around the edges.
Gently stir, fold, or leave them whole—depending on whether you want soft scrambled whites or an omelet-style shape.
Continue cooking for another 1–2 minutes until the egg whites are fully set and no longer runny.
Remove from heat and serve immediately.
